title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Measuring Certificate Money Still Held
content:
Once the paying certificate of deposit is known, the portion of a Savings & Money Market Accounts product that still counts as that certificate's money is fixed by the definition below, together with the ceiling on what may actually leave.

## Definition

**Paid in by the certificate.** Add together all deposits to this account that came from that certificate. They reach the account as internal transfers from it, and they take in the certificate's interest payouts as well as its payout at maturity or during the grace period.

**Sent back to the certificate.** Add together all withdrawals from this account whose receiving side was that same certificate.

**Net certificate money.** The first total less the second. A negative figure is treated as zero.

**Amount moved.** The lower of the net certificate money and the funds standing in the account at the instant the transfer is made, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Excluded.** Money that reached the account from any other source, and interest the savings or money market account earned on its own, never form part of the figure and are not moved.

## Worked example (hypothetical entries)

| Entry | Amount |
|---|---|
| Interest payout from the certificate | 120.50 |
| Second interest payout from the certificate | 95.25 |
| Maturity payout from the certificate | 10250.00 |
| Earlier withdrawal sent back to the certificate | 500.00 |
| Deposit received by ACH credit | 1800.00 |
| Savings interest credited by the account itself | 14.10 |

- Paid in by the certificate: 120.50 plus 95.25 plus 10250.00, making 10465.75.
- Less the 500.00 sent back: 9965.75 of net certificate money.
- The ACH credit and the account's own interest play no part.
- With 8000.00 standing in the account, the lower figure governs and 8000.00 is moved. With 12000.00 standing in it, 9965.75 is moved.

## Points of judgement

**Could more leave than the certificate put in?** No. The net certificate money is itself a ceiling, and the funds in the account can only lower it.

**The certificate has received back more than it paid in. What is moved?** Nothing, since the net figure is taken as zero.
